experience.player_does: Launch the game, press Play, use F4 to cycle through six temporary cell pitches while panning across the world, and use F3 to show an explicit scale ID and numeric cell size alongside performance stats so a preferred option can be reported precisely.
experience.feels_like: The same world remains intact while its presentation scale changes immediately, making it easy to judge smaller cells against navigational context rather than infer a choice from a static image. After a preference is chosen, the experiment checkpoint can be rolled back and the selected pitch reimplemented without the debug controls.
experience.camera: Keep the existing fixed 1920x1080 logical view, smooth panning, world bounds, and Home reset; change only the cell pitch used by the presentation.
experience.controls: F4 advances through scale IDs S1 through S6 for 6, 8, 10, 12, 15, and 20 logical units per cell and wraps to the first; F3 continues to toggle performance stats and prints both `Scale ID: S#` and `Cell size: # units`; arrow keys and Home remain unchanged.
experience.not_this: Not a final scale decision, persisted user setting, zoom system, redesigned camera, or permanent debug control; this is a throwaway checkpoint whose debug code will be removed after the preference is selected.

design_refs.why: The end state requires the world to remain readable at different distances while routes, boundaries, and landmarks survive; this probe supplies direct evidence for the unresolved fullscreen scale question.
The probe changes only presentation density while preserving the same cell grammar and compositions for judging readability.

mockup.not_possible: The question is the live readability and navigational feel of several scales while panning; a static vector mockup would not represent that interaction.

considered_existing.why_not: It already owns the fixed logical viewport, camera offset, cell pitch, debug overlay, and world drawing, so extending it avoids introducing a second renderer or debug subsystem.
The map data must remain unchanged; cell pitch is presentation state and does not belong in the typed persisted map boundary.

modules.role: Own the temporary presentation-only cell-scale cycle alongside the existing camera and performance debug controls.
modules.why: The unresolved scale question needs a live comparison in the existing world surface without adding a new module or changing authored content.
modules.boundary_data: Reads typed LevelFormat data and changes only local presentation values; no scale choice crosses into map data or logic.

files.why: Add the reversible F4 pitch cycle and recalculate the camera bounds and cell rendering from the active temporary pitch while leaving F3 performance stats intact.

functions.why: Recalculate the bounded camera offset when the temporary pitch changes and continue the existing smooth presentation pan.
Handle F4 as the reversible pitch-cycle action without repurposing F3 or introducing a persistent input action.
Render the existing field and debug overlay using the currently selected temporary cell pitch.

functions.signature: func _draw_map_cell(layer: LevelLayer, column: int, row: int) -> void
functions.why: Place each existing cell using the active probe pitch while preserving the current map colors, shapes, and camera offset behavior.

revisions.what: Expanded the experiment description to state the comparison flow, the post-choice rollback and reimplementation step, and the scale ID shown in the performance overlay.
revisions.why: Human review found the generated plan too status-heavy and asked for a clear free-form explanation of how the experiment works and how the temporary code will be removed.

revisions.what: Reduced the probe range to six pitches at or below the original 20-unit reference and made the overlay label the numeric cell size explicitly.
revisions.why: The human found 12 units preferable, requested smaller comparisons, rejected candidates larger than the original 20-unit pitch, and reiterated that the size itself must be visible on screen.
